title: Force Index spike-magnitude and directional-asymmetry refinements
description: Force Index is already implemented (2-day EMA for entries, 13-day for trend confirmation) matching docs/Analyse.md, but Elder ch. 30 has additional, more specific rules not yet in the codebase. (1) A distinct, simpler spike definition -- '5 times or more its usual depth' -- for a short-term reversal signal, different from and additional to the existing Screen-2 `_is_force_index_spike` (1.0x trailing-13-bar standard deviation, itself a `decisions`-recorded choice since the book gives no numeric spike definition for THAT specific usage). (2) An explicit, stated directional asymmetry: down-spikes reliably predict rallies (fear is short-lived) but up-spikes do NOT reliably predict declines (greed persists longer) -- the existing `_is_force_index_spike` currently applies the identical 1-stdev test symmetrically to both directions. This task requires a real methodology decision, not just new code: should the bearish/overbought-rally spike condition use a stricter threshold than the bullish/oversold-pullback one?

checklist.step: DECIDE AND RECORD whether to add the '5x usual depth' rule as a second, separate signal alongside the existing Screen-2 stdev-based spike check, or treat it as a reason to revisit that existing threshold -- these are genuinely different scopes.

DECIDE AND RECORD whether/how to encode the directional asymmetry (stricter threshold for bearish spikes than bullish ones, given Elder's explicit claim they aren't equally reliable) -- run this past the verify-elder-signal skill given it changes existing signal behavior.
Implement whichever of the above was decided, with unit tests covering both directions explicitly (not just one, given the asymmetry is the whole point).
Update docs/Analyse.md §2/§4 to document the refined rule(s) and the asymmetry rationale.
